faq.q: Which vehicles can use the smart socket?
faq.a: It is designed for 2-, 3- and 4-wheelers that charge from a standard AC socket using their own portable charger. We confirm compatibility for your vehicle mix during the site assessment.
Yes. Charging is started, monitored and paid for in the Atom EV app, which is how the socket controls access.

faq.q: Is it suitable for outdoor parking?
faq.a: The enclosure rating is being confirmed against the current datasheet. For exposed outdoor bays we will recommend a protected location or an IP54 product such as the wallbox.

features.title: Three ways to start
features.text: Easy mode, an RFID card or the Bluetooth app. Only registered users can charge when access control is on.

features.title: Scheduled charging

features.title: Built-in safety
features.text: Integrated surge protection plus earth-fault, leakage, short-circuit and over-temperature protection.

features.title: IP54, rust-free enclosure

useCases.title: Apartments & societies

rows: Atom EV app (Bluetooth) or RFID card

faq.q: Will a 22 kW wallbox charge my car at 22 kW?
faq.a: Only if the car's on-board charger and your supply support three-phase 22 kW. Many cars accept 7.4 or 11 kW on AC, so we size the wallbox to the vehicle and the connection.

faq.q: Can residents in a society share wallboxes?
faq.a: Yes. RFID cards or the app identify each user, so shared points can be used by registered residents only.

faq.q: Does it need an internet connection?
faq.a: No. The wallbox is controlled over Bluetooth from the app, and RFID works locally.

faq.q: How is this different from the wallbox?
faq.a: The destination charger is built for shared, commercial use: it can have two guns, stands on a pedestal, and connects to a charging management system over Ethernet, Wi-Fi or 4G.

faq.q: Can it connect to our charging management system?
faq.a: OCPP 1.6J is available as an option. We confirm backend compatibility for your platform before the order.
Type 2 (IEC 62196). Other AC connector standards are confirmed per order against the current datasheet.

faq.q: Which power band do I need?
faq.a: It depends on how long vehicles stay, how many charge at once and the supply at your site. Quick-stop public sites usually need more power per gun than depots charging overnight. We size it after a site assessment.
Vehicles that use the CCS2 connector, which most new electric cars in India use. Compatibility for buses and commercial vehicles is confirmed per model.

faq.q: Will my site need a new transformer?
faq.a: Often, for higher power bands. The survey covers available load, DISCOM approvals and any transformer or civil works, and the quote states them separately.

sections.note: Every quote states its inclusions and exclusions: utility upgrades, transformer, civil work, permits, network connectivity, payment/CMS, taxes and warranty.

items.q: Do you only supply chargers, or install them too?
items.a: Both. We can supply chargers alone, supply and install, or deliver the complete site including civil and electrical works.

items.q: What happens during a site assessment?
items.a: We check the available power and load, the parking layout, cable routes and the civil and electrical scope, then recommend chargers and a phased plan.

items.q: Who handles DISCOM approvals and transformer upgrades?
items.a: We include them in the survey and state them separately in the quote, so you can see what the charger costs and what the site needs.

items.q: Can we start small and add chargers later?
items.a: Yes. We design the electrical scope with expansion in mind, so later chargers don't mean starting over.

items.q: What support do you provide after launch?
items.a: Preventive maintenance, fault triage and service escalation, with AMC and managed-operations options. Service levels are agreed in the contract.
